To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+3}{{x}^{2}+x-6} \\  & =\frac{x+3}{(x+3)(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x+3}}{\cancel{(x+3)}(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
x-2=0
$$

This gives the solution $x=2.$ 

Therefore, the equation of the vertical asymptote is $x=2.$
